blocks.prompt: 9. Sikander starts saving Rs. 500 in the first month and plans to increase his savings [printed as 'plan to increase your savings'] by Rs. 500 each month thereafter. He wants to determine if he will have saved at least Rs. 12,000 by the end of 24 months. Use mathematical induction to justify whether his savings plan will meet this goal.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh rozmarra ka sawal hai: pehle \(n\) mahine baad kul bachat ka formula nikalna hai, usay induction se saabit karna hai, aur phir \(n = 24\) rakh kar goal se muqabla karna hai.
Pehle mahine 500, doosre mahine 1000, teesre mahine 1500 bachaye: yani \(m\)th mahine mein \(500m\). Har mahine ki bachat 500 barhti hai, jaise kitab ke Ali wale push-ups example mein roz push-ups barhte the.
Note: kitab ke sawal mein "his" ki jagah ghalti se "your savings" chhapa hai; matlab Sikander ki bachat hi hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: pehle mahine ki bachat Rs. 500; har mahine ki bachat pichhle mahine se Rs. 500 zyada.
Maloom karna hai: kya 24 mahine ke aakhir tak kul bachat kam az kam Rs. 12,000 hogi?
Tareeqa: Pehle \(T(n)\), yani \(n\) mahine ki kul bachat, ka formula; phir mathematical induction se saboot; aakhir mein \(n = 24\).

Formula nikalein
\[T(n) = 500 + 1000 + \cdots + 500n\]
\[= 500(1 + 2 + \cdots + n)\]
\[= 500 \cdot \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2}\]
\[= 250n(n + 1)\]
Kyun: \(m\)th mahine ki bachat \(500m\) hai, is liye har term mein 500 common nikala. Pehle \(n\) counting numbers ka jama \(\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}\) hota hai (yeh A.P. ka sum hai). Phir \(500 \div 2 = 250\).

Statement aur mahana rule
\[S(n): T(n) = 250n(n + 1)\]
\[T(k + 1) = T(k) + 500(k + 1)\]
Kyun: \(k + 1\) mahine ki kul bachat = \(k\) mahine ki kul bachat + \((k + 1)\)th mahine ki bachat, jo \(500(k + 1)\) hai. Yeh rule inductive step mein kaam aayega.

Base case: \(n = 1\)
\[T(1) = 500\]
\[250 \times 1 \times 2 = 500\]
Is liye \(S(1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: Pehle mahine ke baad us ke paas Rs. 500 hain, aur formula bhi 500 deta hai.

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein
\[T(k) = 250k(k + 1) \quad (A)\]
Kyun: Farz kiya ke \(k\) mahine baad formula sahi kul bachat deta hai.

Inductive step: pehle rule, phir (A)
\[T(k + 1) = 250k(k + 1) + 500(k + 1)\]
\[= 250(k + 1)(k + 2)\]
\[= 250(k + 1)[(k + 1) + 1]\]
Is liye \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: Rule mein \(T(k)\) ki jagah (A) rakha. Dono hisson mein \(250(k + 1)\) common hai (kyunke \(500 = 250 \times 2\)), bahar nikala to bracket mein \(k + 2\) bacha. \(k + 2 = (k + 1) + 1\), yani yeh bilkul \(n = k + 1\) wala formula hai.

Saboot ka conclusion
\(S(1)\) sahi hai aur \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of mathematical induction se \(T(n) = 250n(n + 1)\) har positive integer \(n\) ke liye sahi hai.
Kyun: Induction ki dono sharten poori ho gayin.

Asal sawal ka jawab: \(n = 24\)
\[T(24) = 250 \times 24 \times 25\]
\[= 150{,}000\]
\[150{,}000 \ge 12{,}000\]
Kyun: "24 mahine ke aakhir tak" ka matlab \(n = 24\). Kul bachat Rs. 150,000 hai, jo goal se bahut zyada (taqreeban 12 guna) hai.
Dhyan dein: Kuch log is sawal ko yun parhte hain ke "kul bachat har mahine 500 barhti hai", yani \(T(n) = 500n\); us soorat mein \(T(24) = 12{,}000\), jo goal ke bilkul barabar hai. Dono soorton mein jawab "haan" hai.

Tasdeeq: table se
\[T(1) = 500,\ T(2) = 1500,\ T(3) = 3000\]
\[250 \times 3 \times 4 = 3000 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(500 + 1000 + 1500 = 3000\), aur formula bhi 3000 deta hai.
blocks.final_answer: Haan. Induction se \(n\) mahine ki kul bachat \(T(n) = 250n(n + 1)\) hai, is liye 24 mahine baad Rs. 150,000 bachenge, jo Rs. 12,000 se zyada hain. Plan goal poora karta hai.
